title: David's Mighty Men
lead: The elite warriors who fought for David, remembered in two lists (2 Samuel 23:8–39; 1 Chronicles 11:10–47): the Three, the Thirty, and their leaders, with short stories of their deeds against the Philistines and the giants of Gath.

sections.b: Many of David's men joined him in the wilderness years, when he gathered the distressed and indebted at the cave of Adullam (1 Samuel 22:1–2). Their deeds are told in short heroic reports: giants of Gath killed (2 Samuel 21:15–22), a stand that held a field, water brought from Bethlehem through enemy lines. The list in 2 Samuel 23 names the Three, Abishai and Benaiah, and the Thirty, ending with Uriah the Hittite; Chronicles' list adds more names and a long account of the men who came to David at Ziklag and Hebron (1 Chronicles 12). Several of them appear elsewhere: Asahel (2 Samuel 2:18–23), Benaiah (1 Kings 2:25–35), Uriah (2 Samuel 11).
